# The flux register, monitor amounts and conservation budgets {#sec-ch10}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@73c45a7c8c991209924e1137992352c335575062 (UCzhangxi/snapy v3/final)

Every face flux of a stage goes through one object per module, the flux register. The hydro module has one, and
so has the scalar module. A producer writes its flux into the register; the register knows which faces are
prescribed walls, books every change it makes to a flux as an amount, counts the events its producers report,
and folds the stages of a step into the step's totals. After a step is accepted, the conservation budget reads
the register and the state. This chapter describes the register's writes in the order a stage makes them, then
how the budget and the cycle line read them. Which faces are walls, and with what values, is the subject of the
boundary chapter (@sec-ch11-reflecting); how a captured stage is replayed is the execution chapter's. The schemes
are listed in @tbl-ch10-schemes.

| scheme | switch | default | order | main test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| posts (@sec-ch10-posts) | none (bookkeeping) | always on | exact (plain adds) | `test_flux_register` |
| prescribed faces and their reapplication (@sec-ch10-prescribed) | a wall boundary condition | on at a wall | exact on the wall face | `test_prescribed_after_sources` |
| the wall batch (@sec-ch10-wallbatch) | none | on with a wall | exact (deterministic sum) | `test_graph_monitor_amounts` |
| amounts and the stage fold (@sec-ch10-amounts) | none | always on | exact recursion | `test_flux_register` |
| monitor counts (@sec-ch10-counts) | none | always on | exact (integer) | `test_fp32_face_floor_counts` |
| rollback and redo, through replay (@sec-ch10-rollback) | none | on a rejected attempt | exact | `test_graph_monitor_amounts` |
| budgets, the budget series and the cycle line (@sec-ch10-budget) | `outputs: - {type: budget}`, `ncycle_out` | off; cycle line every `ncycle_out` | round-off | `test_budget` |

: The schemes of this chapter. Test names omit the `.release` and `_python` suffixes of their ctest entries.
